summary: 58-year-old woman: adjusted calcium 2.86 mmol/L with inappropriately high PTH, kidney stone, radius T-score −2.7, eGFR 55, on bendroflumethiazide. Fifth International Workshop 2022: several surgical indications → parathyroidectomy (localisation once surgery is decided); exclude FHH; review the thiazide.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Raised calcium on blood tests and tiredness
inputs.hpi: Referred with raised calcium found when checked for tiredness and low mood. Passed a kidney stone last year. Fractured wrist after a trip 2 years ago. Thirsty, passing more urine. On bendroflumethiazide for blood pressure. No family history of high calcium.

imaging.name: USS kidneys
imaging.result: Two non-obstructing calculi in the left kidney. No hydronephrosis.

imaging.name: DEXA
imaging.result: T-scores: lumbar spine −1.9, total hip −2.1, distal third radius −2.7 (osteoporosis).

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Primary hyperparathyroidism with surgical indications (osteoporosis, nephrolithiasis, eGFR <60)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Primary hyperparathyroidism (adjusted Ca 2.86, PTH 11.8) meeting several surgical criteria: nephrolithiasis, distal radius T-score −2.7, eGFR 55. Stop the thiazide (switch antihypertensive), check urine calcium:creatinine clearance ratio to exclude FHH, then localisation (US + sestamibi) for parathyroidectomy.

mustExclude.note: A parathyroid patient's documented plan must not contain a thyroidectomy operation or lifelong levothyroxine (wrong operation in the record).
mustExclude.proposedFix: Add a Parathyroid dx-variant group (E21, primary_hyperparathyroidism, parathyroid_adenoma) ahead of Thyroid, and match baseDiagnosis/keywords on word boundaries.

mustInclude.note: Fifth Workshop 2022: parathyroidectomy is indicated when any criterion is met; this patient meets three.
Thiazides raise serum calcium; the patient takes one. The plan must address it.

guideline.name: Fifth International Workshop — evaluation and management of primary hyperparathyroidism
guideline.section: Diagnosis (PTH, exclude FHH, vitamin D); surgical indications (serum calcium >0.25 mmol/L above ULN, osteoporosis T-score ≤−2.5 or vertebral fracture, eGFR <60 mL/min, nephrolithiasis/nephrocalcinosis, hypercalciuria, age <50); localisation only once surgery is decided
guideline.citation: Bilezikian JP, Khan AA, Silverberg SJ, et al. Evaluation and management of primary hyperparathyroidism: summary statement and guidelines from the Fifth International Workshop. J Bone Miner Res. 2022;37:2293–2314.

guideline.name: Society for Endocrinology emergency guidance — acute hypercalcaemia in adults
guideline.section: Severe or symptomatic hypercalcaemia: IV 0.9% saline rehydration, IV bisphosphonate after rehydration, stop contributing drugs, monitor renal function
guideline.citation: Walsh J, Gittoes N, Selby P; Society for Endocrinology Clinical Committee. Society for Endocrinology Endocrine Emergency Guidance: Emergency management of acute hypercalcaemia in adult patients. Endocr Connect. 2016;5:G9–G11.

rationale: Base parathyroid case. Symptoms are non-specific (fatigue, thirst); the diagnosis comes from labs. The one critical expectation is drug safety (thiazide in hypercalcaemia).
